# SOC-C13 eligibility proposal (A2, candidate)

Study: Forrester, D., Lynch, A., Bostock, L., Newlands, F., Preston, B., & Cary, A. (2017). Family Safeguarding Hertfordshire: Evaluation report (July 2017). Children's Social Care Innovation Programme Evaluation Report 55. London: Department for Education (DFE-RR574, ISBN 978-1-78105-635-6).

Title page check: title "Family Safeguarding Hertfordshire Evaluation Report", July 2017, authors Donald Forrester (CASCADE, Cardiff), Amy Lynch, Lisa Bostock, Fiona Newlands, Bart Preston, Alex Cary (Tilda Goldberg Centre, University of Bedfordshire) (p.1). Matches the given reference; the series number (Evaluation Report 55) and DfE reference (DFE-RR574, p.96) are added.

Text: supplied PDF (96 pages), converted with pdftotext -layout to _text/full.txt; _text/paged.txt prefixes each line with the PDF page. Printed page numbers equal PDF page numbers. Figures 1-10 (graphs, case-study diagrams) are images and are not in the extracted text.

Proposal: eligible.

## Criterion 1: relationship in a public or publicly funded service
- Object: Family Safeguarding Hertfordshire, a whole-system reform of a local authority's Children's Services with police, health, probation and substance misuse partners (p.9, p.16).
- Relationships studied: between social workers and families (coded observations of worker-family meetings, p.35-37; parents' ratings and accounts of their relationship with the worker, p.38-39) and among professionals in multidisciplinary teams (adult workers, group supervision, p.24-25, p.48-49).
- Public service: Hertfordshire County Council Children's Services and partner agencies; funded under the DfE Children's Social Care Innovation Programme (p.1, p.96).

## Criterion 2: at least one qualitative and one quantitative finding
- Qualitative: themes from staff interviews (61 staff, p.24-27, Table 15 p.73), open-ended survey and parent interview responses (p.29-30, p.38-39), 10 case studies (p.44-45), observation of 8 group supervisions (p.48-49).
- Quantitative: staff survey at 3 time points (439 returns, p.27-31), coded observations of practice with t-tests and correlations (Table 2 p.36-37, Table 25 p.82), parent outcome measures (Table 3 p.40, Table 5 p.42), ICS records for 447 families (Table 4 p.41), KPI dataset for 940 families (p.50-58), cost estimates (p.59-61).

Both criteria are met. Joint claims were not used as a criterion.
